Action Plan:
1. Start Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented) in addition to current Paracetamol for acute headache relief.  
2. Maintain good oral hydration throughout the day.  
3. Arrange a blood-pressure check within the next few days (e.g., local pharmacy, practice nurse).  
4. Purchase/obtain a home thermometer to monitor for fever.  
5. Monitor for red-flag symptoms (worsening severity, fever, skin rash, neurological deficits); seek urgent review if any develop.  
6. If headaches persist, recur, or appear related to menstrual cycle or other triggers, book follow-up for further assessment and possible migraine management plan.  
7. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Reason for visit: New-onset severe headache, 1-day duration.  
• History of presenting complaint:  
  – Onset yesterday morning on waking; left-sided, throbbing, intensity fluctuates but never fully resolves.  
  – Photophobia present.  
  – No nausea, vomiting, visual disturbance, abnormal smells/tastes.  
  – No fever noted (temperature not measured).  
  – No positional, cough, or sneeze exacerbation; feels better lying down.  
  – No limb weakness, numbness, or tingling.  
• Past medical history: Denies significant illnesses, hospitalisations, or surgeries.  
• Medications:  
  – Microgynon oral contraceptive (dose/frequency not documented; taken for 6 years).  
  – Paracetamol (OTC, dose/frequency not documented).  
• Allergies: Aspirin – causes marked nausea.  
• Family history: Mother – hypertension, migraines.  
• Social history: Lives with housemates. Alcohol: a few drinks on weekends. Non-smoker. Denies illicit drug use.

Objective:
(Consult conducted via telehealth; no physical examination performed.)  
• No vital signs recorded.  
• No skin changes or rashes reported by patient.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute unilateral throbbing headache
   - Assessment: Probable first-episode migraine.
   - Differential diagnosis: Tension-type headache, sinus headache, medication-overuse headache, secondary causes (e.g., intracranial pathology) – less likely given current presentation but to be monitored.
   - Investigations planned: None immediately; arrange blood-pressure check; advise temperature monitoring at home.
   - Treatment planned: Add Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented) with ongoing Paracetamol; ensure adequate hydration.
   - Relevant referrals: None at present; consider neurology referral if headaches become persistent or atypical.

Quality checks:
● Missing but expected elements: Objective vitals (BP, temperature); detailed dosage for Paracetamol and advised Ibuprofen; full allergy list beyond Aspirin not discussed.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; minimal background noise, no significant inaudible sections.
